### Day 18: 1 Samuel 16:14–23
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-18-1-samuel-16-1423.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 16:18
Points:
- Scripture presents David in two unexpected, complementary roles: a sensitive musician and a courageous warrior.
- Relieving Saul’s torment required more than musical technique; David played with genuine tenderness that ministered to the soul.
- Tenderness and strength are not contradictory traits, but essential qualities that create true personal wholeness.
- David’s dual character reflects Jesus Christ, who is both the tenderhearted creator and the triumphant warrior.

### David’s Ministry to Saul
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/davids-ministry-to-saul
Passage: 1 Samuel 16:23
Points:
- David entered royal service to minister to the suffering king whom he was destined to replace.
- Saul’s affliction under a distressing spirit illustrates that God sovereignly rules over all circumstances, including painful judgments.
- David was recommended not merely for his musical skill and bravery, but because the Lord was with him.
- Living in the royal palace providentially trained David to understand the responsibilities and pitfalls of leadership.
- God's sovereignty over affliction provides comfort, assuring believers that He works all things toward their ultimate good.
